name: Read
description:
Read one local or configured virtual-filesystem path or registered lightweight resource. Use multiple calls for multiple targets. Local output is mode-aware: Hashline mode adds a [PATH#TAG] header to non-raw editable files and records the actual raw/non-raw range as seen; Replace mode uses ordinary numbered output. Virtual-filesystem and registered-resource reads are always read-only and never create an editable snapshot. Path selectors select line ranges.

Supported targets include local paths, artifact://<id>, skill:// resources, rule:// resources, and session://current resources. A full result may be truncated; request a narrower selector when exact lines are known. Full reads above the configured limit are answered with a preview; large files require a line-range selector.

Read accepts exactly one parameter: `path`. Line ranges go inside the path selector (`path:1-200`, `path:10+5`, `path:raw`); do not invent other parameter names (e.g. `selector`, `path_sel`, `offset`, `limit`).

path.description: File path or registered resource URL to read. Supports local paths, artifact://<id>, skill://list, skill://list/all, skill://<name>, skill://<name>/<relative-path>, rule://<name>, and session://current resources including session://current/history. Append path selectors such as :10-20, :10+5, or :raw for ranges/raw output.

name: Glob
description: Discover paths through the configured filesystem backend with ripgrep-style rg --files -g semantics. Patterns are passed as a single rg -g override glob: *.rs matches recursively by file name, src/*.rs matches one level under src, src/**/*.rs matches recursively, and !pattern excludes matches. Use multiple calls for independent patterns.

pattern.description: A single rg -g override glob, for example *.rs, **/*.rs, **/*.docx, **/*.*, src/**/*.ts, or !target/**. Bare file-name globs such as *.rs match recursively like ripgrep.

path.description: Optional directory to search from. Defaults to .

name: Grep
description: Search content through the configured filesystem backend or a registered resource URL such as session://current/history. Local Hashline mode groups results per editable file under [PATH#TAG]; Replace mode and read-only backends use ripgrep-style path:line:match output. Resource paths do not accept selectors or globs. Use context to identify exact target ranges, a single rg -g override glob to restrict filesystem targets, and multiple calls for independent patterns.

pattern.description: The Rust regular expression pattern to search for. For literal symbols, simple names usually work directly; escape regex metacharacters when needed.

path.description: File, directory, or registered resource URL to search. Defaults to .

glob.description: A single rg -g override glob to filter files (e.g. "*.rs", "**/*.docx", "src/**/*.ts", "*.{ts,tsx}", or "!target/**"). Bare file-name globs such as *.rs match recursively like ripgrep.

context.description: Number of lines before and after each match. In Hashline mode, each editable local file group includes its own [PATH#TAG] and only complete displayed match/context lines become seen; Replace and read-only backends retain ordinary search output.

name: Write
description: Create or fully overwrite a file on the local filesystem. Parent directories are created automatically. This operation never writes to an injected read-only virtual filesystem.

path.description: Path to the file to write

content.description: Content to write to the file

name: Edit
description:
Apply a hashline edit. The runtime-selected Edit mode replaces this catalog template before exposing it to the model.

Common mistakes: `PUT18.=18:` is parsed as `PUT 18.=18:` (missing space is accepted), but ranges must be start<=end and stay inside the file; unified-diff or apply_patch syntax is never valid.

Choose locators by scope: `N.=M` line numbers for small precise ranges; `'start'..'end'` anchor line texts (from the latest Read output) for wide or structural ranges or when boundaries are easy to miss (e.g. closing braces). Anchors must match exactly one line after trimming.

name: Bash
description: Execute a focused shell command in the current session working directory for build, test, version-control, package-manager, server, or other shell-only tasks. Returns stdout and stderr. Commands classified as ordinary file reading, content search, or path discovery may be rejected by runtime policy.

command.description: The focused shell command to execute.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. If the command exceeds this duration, it will be killed. Only set this for commands expected to need a non-default duration (e.g. build, test, server start). Default: global tool timeout from configuration, clamped to 5-600 seconds.

name: Python
description: Execute Python code directly on the host system with network, subprocess, filesystem, and C-extension access. Returns stdout and stderr. Suitable for data processing, analysis, or helper scripts that require the host Python ecosystem.

script_file.description: Path to a Python file to execute. Provide either 'script' or 'script_file', not both.

name: TodoRead
description: Read the persisted task list for the current session, including its revision and stable item IDs. Completed items are omitted by default.

include_completed.description: Whether to include completed items in the result. Defaults to false.

name: TodoWrite
description: Apply an atomic incremental update to the persisted task list for the current session. Updates use the current revision and stable item IDs to prevent stale writes.

base_revision.description: The revision on which this update is based.

add.description: New items to append. Every new item starts pending.

content.description: A short, concrete, actionable task description.

update.description: Content replacements for existing non-completed items identified by stable ID.

remove.description: Stable IDs of non-active items to delete. Pause or complete active items first.

name: TodoAdvance
description: Atomically transition persisted todo progress. Complete or pause active items, activate pending items, or reopen completed items. Multiple related items may transition together.

base_revision.description: The revision on which these transitions are based.

complete.description: In-progress item IDs whose outcomes have been verified.

activate.description: Pending item IDs to make part of the active batch.

pause.description: In-progress item IDs to return to pending.

reopen.description: Completed item IDs to return to pending.

name: PlanDraft
description: Create, replace, or cancel the current plan draft. Use this for the complete proposed plan and for every revision before explicit user confirmation. Pass an empty content string when the user explicitly cancels or abandons planning. This tool does not confirm the plan.

content.description: The complete plan draft in Markdown. Pass an empty string to cancel the unconfirmed draft.

name: PlanConfirm
description: Confirm and lock in the current plan draft. Call this ONLY when the user explicitly confirms the plan. Do NOT call this during drafting or when the user requests changes — only on explicit confirmation.

name: PlanClear
description: Clear the current plan. Call this when the current plan is fully completed and all tasks are done. After calling this, the system prompt will no longer include the plan section.

name: SubAgent
description:
Launches a sub-agent that runs independently. The sub-agent executes the given prompt as an isolated agent session. Results are batched: ALL sub-agents complete before results are presented together. Use this for delegating sub-tasks that can run in parallel.

Fork mode: pass fork=true to inherit parent session context (conversation history, plan, skills). Default is a fresh independent session.

prompt.description: The prompt/task to delegate to the sub-agent

description.description: Short description of the sub-agent task (for logging)

fork.description: Set to true to inherit parent session context (conversation history, plan, skills). Default is false for a fresh independent session.

name: PythonSandbox
description: Execute Python code in a CPython WASI sandbox with restricted permissions — only specific directories have read/write access. No subprocess, no network, no C extensions. Full CPython standard library available (json/csv/re/math/datetime/xml etc.). Use this for safe execution of untrusted or sensitive Python code.

script_file.description: Path to a Python file to execute. Provide either 'script' or 'script_file', not both.
